crossRefs.note: Remember me, my God, for good, all that I have done for this people.
My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning?
God, you are my God. I will earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary…
“Hear, our God; for we are despised. Turn back their reproach on their own head. Give them up for a plunder in a land…
Don’t cover their iniquity. Don’t let their sin be blotted out from before you; for they have insulted the builders.”
Remember them, my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
Don’t let the foot of pride come against me. Don’t let the hand of the wicked drive me away.
There the workers of iniquity are fallen. They are thrust down, and shall not be able to rise.
The proud have hidden a snare for me, they have spread the cords of a net by the path. They have set traps for me.

people.name: Sanballat
people.line: Governor of Samaria, opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem

people.name: Tobiah
people.line: Ammonite official who opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding efforts

translations.web: “Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their works, and also the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets, that would have put me in fear.”
translations.bsb: O my God, remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they have done, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the other prophets who tried to intimidate me.
translations.kjv: My God, think thou upon Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their works, and on the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets, that would have put me in fear.
translations.asv: Remember, O my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their works, and also the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets, that would have put me in fear.
